clue.text: No bill is sent back to the staff

indicators.note: sent back tells us to read the run of the two words No and bill from right to left

parts.note: taken as written
a tab is a bill, as in a bar tab

explanation.surface: A rejected bill is returned to the office workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns the whole run NOTAB around. 'Staff' looks like employees but is a rod, the sense the definition needs.
explanation.definitionFit: A baton is a short stick or rod, such as a conductor's or a relay runner's.

clue.text: Played the violin vigorously, despite being care-laden

explanation.surface: A violinist plays with energy despite being weighed down with worries.
explanation.definitionFit: A violinist draws the bow hard down the strings; someone weighed down by troubles is burdened and oppressed.

clue.text: Your tyre needs air-no doubt about it!

explanation.surface: A motorist is told bluntly their tyre is deflated, no question.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyre wanting air is deflated; a flat statement is definite and leaves no room for argument.

clue.text: Want Edward to be full of energy

indicators.note: to be full of says the name holds the next piece within it

parts.note: Ned is a short form of the name Edward
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone wishes Edward were more lively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be full of' puts E inside NED.
explanation.definitionFit: To want something is to lack or require it, a synonym.

clue.text: Remind people how to raise a fire alarm

definitions.text: how to raise a fire alarm

explanation.surface: Advice on alerting others, whether jogging memories or warning of fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Something familiar jogs the memory; old fire alarms were raised by sounding a hand bell.

clue.text: Resolution I've made to make drastic changes

indicators.note: made in the sense of fashioned anew, so the letters are worked into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A personal resolution is formed to overhaul one's life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges RESOLUTION plus IVE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To revolutionise is to transform something completely, an overhaul at root level.

clue.text: Butler supports a Middle Easterner

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece supporting another sits below it

parts.note: Rab Butler was a prominent British Conservative politician of the mid twentieth century

explanation.surface: A household butler works for a man from the Gulf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supports' puts RAB beneath A in this down entry. RAB Butler was a British Chancellor and Home Secretary.
explanation.definitionFit: An Arab is a person from the Arabic-speaking peoples of the Middle East.

clue.text: English monarch just managing to get by

parts.note: a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A British king barely scraping a living.
explanation.definitionFit: Eking out means making scant resources last, surviving narrowly.

clue.text: Many a remarkable person is the solitary type

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, crossword shorthand for many
a oner is British slang for an exceptional, one-of-a-kind person

explanation.surface: Many outstanding people prefer their own company.
explanation.walkthrough: ONER is British slang for someone unique or outstanding.
explanation.definitionFit: A loner is someone who keeps apart from others by choice.

clue.text: Sounds as though you and I have to make cloth

indicators.note: Sounds as though tells us the word spoken resembles the entry when said

parts.note: you and I have is the contraction we've

explanation.surface: Two people seem obliged to produce fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: WE'VE is spoken just like the word for making cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: To weave is to interlace threads on a loom, producing fabric.

clue.text: Six given second-rate allowance shiver

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
B grade is second-rate
a ration is a fixed allowance

explanation.surface: Six people are handed a poor portion and tremble.
explanation.definitionFit: A shiver is a quick trembling motion, a kind of quivering.

clue.text: Courting disaster

parts.note: read not as inviting trouble but as a calamity in courtship, a love affair gone wrong

explanation.definitionFit: A courtship that collapses is a failed love affair, a disaster in wooing.

clue.text: Record which is held by district commissioner

indicators.note: held by places one piece within the other, the outer one doing the holding

explanation.surface: An official keeps hold of a document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'which' is only a link; 'Record' means a gramophone disc, not a written note.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc is a gramophone record, a vinyl recording.

clue.text: A backward moron, but supercilious

indicators.note: backward means the word for moron is read in reverse

parts.note: a fool is a moron

explanation.surface: A slow-witted person who is nevertheless snooty.
explanation.definitionFit: Supercilious and aloof both describe a cool, distant, haughty manner.

clue.text: A needlefish served with seaweed jelly

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish also called a needlefish

explanation.surface: A fish dish is served with a jelly made from seaweed.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar is a gelatinous substance extracted from red algae, used in cooking and labs.

clue.text: We object in middle age to exercising

parts.note: us is the object form of we

indicators.note: middle picks the central letter of the following word

explanation.surface: People protest that they're made to work out in middle age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We object' is grammar, not protest: the object case of 'we' is US.
explanation.definitionFit: Using a power or right is exercising it, synonyms.

clue.text: Feature about a retail group

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the next

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature

explanation.surface: A news feature about a group of shops.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain is a group of shops under one owner.

clue.text: Fail to cotton on!

parts.note: read literally, failing to attach to cotton, mislaying one's yarn, as well as failing to understand

explanation.definitionFit: To lose track of a line of argument is to stop following what is being said.

clue.text: Views a suite, and finishes with visual fatigue

parts.note: eyes as a verb means views
a train is a suite or retinue of attendants

explanation.surface: Someone inspects a hotel suite and ends up with tired eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suite' means a retinue, not rooms; 'and finishes with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Overworking the eyes causes tiredness and discomfort in sight.

clue.text: Called for ophthalmic lotion to be dispensed

explanation.surface: Someone visited to get eye drops administered.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying a casual visit is calling; eye drops are put into the eye.

clue.text: Reply to assurance request from one on death row? Never!

definitions.text: Reply to assurance request from one on death row

explanation.surface: A condemned prisoner is refused a promise, flatly.
explanation.definitionFit: Asked to swear 'on your life', a doomed man might baulk; the phrase is also an emphatic refusal.

clue.text: Instant credit

explanation.surface: A shop offers credit immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: A moment is a split second; buying on account is buying on credit.

clue.text: Swelling requires check-up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for check is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to rebut is to check or repel

explanation.surface: A lump requires a medical examination.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuber is a rounded swelling or protuberance, in anatomy as well as botany.

clue.text: Uncorrupted Conservative carrying little weight

parts.note: lean means thin, with little fat on the body

explanation.surface: An honest Tory politician with little influence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying little weight' suggests lack of influence but means thin.
explanation.definitionFit: Clean means honest and free of corruption.

clue.text: Bohemian girl taken around a US resort

indicators.note: taken around means the name goes round the next piece

parts.note: Mimi is the heroine of Puccini's opera La Boheme

explanation.surface: A free-spirited woman is shown round a Florida holiday city.
explanation.definitionFit: Miami is a Florida city famous for beach holidays.

clue.text: Measure to overthrow blue-eyed boys

indicators.note: to overthrow is to turn upside down, so the word is read the other way

parts.note: pets are favourites, blue-eyed boys

explanation.surface: Steps taken to topple the boss's favourites.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is a measure or action taken to achieve something.

clue.text: Make no changes in Buddhist ethics

indicators.note: in tells us the entry is tucked inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Buddhist moral codes should be kept as they are.
explanation.definitionFit: Stet is a proofreader's mark meaning let it stand, leave unaltered.

clue.text: The Spanish in charge of secular affairs

parts.note: la is the Spanish feminine word for the

explanation.surface: Spaniards running worldly matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Laic means lay, belonging to the laity rather than the clergy.

clue.text: Hibernate in order to get inspiration

indicators.note: put in order means the letters of the word are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: An animal sleeps through winter to find creative ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspiration in physiology is drawing air into the lungs.

clue.text: Conflict in the Christian era requires judicial decision

indicators.note: in places the conflict word inside the era abbreviation

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the Christian era
war is conflict

explanation.surface: Fighting in modern times calls for a ruling from the courts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'requires' is only a link joining wordplay to definition; 'the Christian era' is the standard pointer to anno Domini.
explanation.definitionFit: An award is a sum or ruling granted by a court or arbitrator.

clue.text: Allowed little time, but managed the business splendidly

explanation.surface: A manager left things late yet still ran the firm brilliantly.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting it fine leaves scant margin; read literally, running a firm well.

clue.text: Round and about sooner or later

parts.note: C, from circa, means about
anon means soon, presently

explanation.surface: A round trip will come about at some point.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a musical round, voices entering in turn with the same melody.
